    optimizer.add(end_times[person] <= 1440)  # End of the day is 24:00 or 1440 minutes

    # Add constraints for travel time
    for prev_person in people:
        prev_location = people[prev_person][0]
        prev_end_time = end_times[prev_person]
        travel_time = travel_times.get((prev_location, location), 1440)  # Default to a large number if no direct travel time
        optimizer.add(Implies(meetings[person] & meetings[prev_person], start_times[person] >= prev_end_time + travel_time))
        optimizer.add(Implies(meetings[person] & meetings[prev_person], current_time <= prev_end_time + travel_time))

# Maximize the number of meetings
optimizer.maximize(Sum([If(meetings[person], 1, 0) for person in people]))

# Check if the problem is solvable
if optimizer.check() == sat:
    model = optimizer.model()
    itinerary = []
    for person, (location, start, end, duration) in people.items():
        if model.evaluate(meetings[person]):
            start_time = model.evaluate(start_times[person]).as_long()
            end_time = model.evaluate(end_times[person]).as_long()
            itinerary.append({
                "action": "meet",
                "person": person,
                "start_time": f"{start_time // 60:02}:{start_time % 60:02}",
                "end_time": f"{end_time // 60:02}:{end_time % 60:02}"
            })
    itinerary.sort(key=lambda x: x["start_time"])
    print({"itinerary": itinerary})
else:
    print("No solution found")

This revised code uses the `Optimize` class from Z3, which allows us to use the `maximize` method to optimize the number of meetings. The constraints are set up to ensure that the travel times and meeting times are respected.
